correctness.rationale: The proof fixes the Euclidean norm, parameter range, defining halfspaces, and all quantifiers. Permutation averaging preserves an inscribed ball via Minkowski averaging and convexity, reducing to a diagonal center. Normalized distances to every subset-sum hyperplane give a one-variable max-min problem. The crossing values a_k are exact; the derivative of f(t)=t(2n+1-t^2)/(2(t+1)) has a strictly decreasing numerator, excluding interior minima and reducing the answer to k=1 or k=m. Active facet inequalities then force uniqueness of the center. The packaged standard-library computation checks 20,298 parameter pairs as a finite consistency test, not as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The Euclidean inradius is a canonical metric invariant of a polytope and is useful for roundness, scaling, conditioning, and comparison with other realizations. Partial permutohedra have an active recent literature on faces, volumes, Ehrhart theory, generalized-permutahedron structure, and parking-function connections, but no inspected source gives this invariant. The formula is not an arbitrary finite slice: it classifies an infinite two-parameter family, proves uniqueness of the optimal center, and exposes a sharp geometric phase transition between total-sum and coordinate-cap tangencies at n=m+sqrt(m).
